title: Evidence habit notebook - Ramita (scratch)
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad for building evidence collection habits and mapping informal keystones to formal controls. Not a final artifact — messy, iterative.

Top-level goals
- get predictable list of evidence files per control (log paths, screenshots, policy pdf names)
- make mini scripts that pull a single CSV for each control owner (so auditors get one artefact)
- identify easy wins (what can be exported in <1hr) vs bigger engineering work

Context notes to self
- Redwood private deployments + dedicated runtime = multiple places evidence can live (cloud logs, on-prem file shares, S3 buckets). Need canonical pointers.
- auditors like reproducible steps: "how to reproduce this export" + sample raw + human-readable summary.

Quick mapping brainstorm (control -> likely evidence examples)
- Access controls (user provisioning / deprovisioning): Active Directory / Okta CSV of deactivated users, recent SCIM logs, onboarding/offboarding ticket links.
  Evidence names: okta-user-deprovision-202601.csv, scim-sync-log-2026-01-30.txt
- MFA enforcement: policy screenshot + policy id + login events showing MFA prompts (timestamped)
  Evidence names: mfa-policy-v2.png, auth-events-mfa-jan2026.csv
- Privileged access review: quarterly spreadsheet of privileged accounts, reviewer sign-off emails (pdf)
  Quick step: reach out to infra to get current iam-privileged.csv
- Key management (KMS/HSM): key rotation runbook, KMS audit trail export, kms-rotation-2026-01.json (if customer private, might be offline)
- Change management: PR list + approvals for infra changes, jira links, changelog artifacts (git tags)
- Logging & retention: cloud logging exports (GCP logs, AWS CloudWatch), retention policy doc, sample logs for an incident date

Evidence collection mini-plan (first-pass)
1) Make a tiny template README per control: source system, raw file name, export command, expected columns, owner, privacy notes.
2) Identify 10 highest-value controls (start with access, logging, change mgmt, kvs/key mgmt, deployment approvals).
3) For each control, run one manual export and attach to folder: /evidence/scratch/<control>/<export>-<date>. Keep copy in my user drive until moved.
4) Turn top 3 exports into bash/python scripts that can run w/ service account and output the CSV and a md summary.

Unresolved questions / blockers
- Who is the canonical owner for KMS evidence in Private deployments? (infra or customer success?) TODO: ping @noah.
- Private deployment logs — do we get full access or only aggregated metrics? Need to confirm with legal & sales for NDA constraints.
- How long can we keep raw audit exports in Google Drive for internal prep? Security asked for minimal copies. Maybe keep hashed obfuscated versions for drafts.

Practical notes & snippets (for later)
- Example sqlite-ish export command for on-prem audit DB: sqlite3 /var/log/audit.db "select * from auth_events where ts > '2026-01-01'" > auth-events-jan2026.csv
- GCP logging export (gcloud): gcloud logging read "resource.type=\"gce_instance\" AND severity>=ERROR" --limit=1000 --format=json > gce-errors-2026-01-15.json
- Okta export: Admin console -> Reports -> System Log -> Export (CSV) -> compress + sha256sum -> store in evidence bucket

Mini playbook: how I will handover an evidence bundle to auditor
- create folder evidence/audits/<control>-<date>/
- include: README.md (what this is, search terms), raw.csv.gz, sample-rows.csv (3 rows), provenance.txt (command + user that ran), redaction-note.txt (if any PII removed), summary.md (one paragraph summary)

Short-term todo (this week)
- [ ] export okta deprovision CSV and put in users/ramita/tmp (target: 2026-02-05) (assigned: me)
- [ ] draft README template for evidence bundles (target: 2026-02-06) (assigned: me/noah)
- [ ] ask infra for iam-privileged.csv (ticket: JIRA-TICKET-3421) (assigned: noah)

Longer items (sprint)
- automate 3 exports into scripts + test in CI (sre/infrastructure help)
- align retention + secure storage policy with security team (Ellie)
- create small UX in console to download an "audit bundle" for a given time window (product/console)

Notes to self (voicey):
- Keep saving imperfect artifacts. Auditors need reproducibility, not prettiness.
- Don't hoard secrets in Drive — if export has secrets, redact and store minimal test rows only.
- When in doubt, timestamp everything and include the export command.

Slack refs and cross-links
- slack thread: #trust-ops -> "evidence-bundle-idea" (pinned messages)
- confluence draft: TrustOps/EvidenceBundleDraft (CONFLUENCE-5872)
- jira: JIRA-TICKET-3421 (privileged account export)

End — will iterate. If I get 5 repeatable bundles, stop hoarding and move to shared drive.
